_about: The default files for each scope, shown on the handbook's Default files page with their contents read from templates/. bin/gen-guide.py fails when a file under templates/ (other than .gitkeep) has no entry here, or an entry names a template that does not exist, so a new template is documented before it ships. Edit here, then run make docs.

scopes.title: Your machine
scopes.summary: Once per developer, outside every repository. install.sh writes them; nothing here is committed anywhere.

files.installedBy: install.sh, only when you have none. Uninstall removes it only while it is byte-identical to the template.
files.purpose: Your personal standing instructions, loaded into every Claude Code session on this machine, in every repository.
files.edit: The first line (your name and role), and your own standing rules. Keep it short: every line is paid for on every turn.
files.keep: The which-skill rule and the report shape; they are what the team's repositories assume.

files.purpose: The tracker and its credentials, the git host, the kit remote and the organisation id, read by the kit's scripts.
files.edit: BEARING_TRACKER and its keys, BEARING_GIT_HOST, BEARING_KIT_REMOTE. The Configuration page explains every key.
files.keep: Its location and mode. It must never be copied into a repository.

files.installedBy: claude plugin, when install.sh or /plugin install adds the Bearing marketplace and enables the plugins.
files.purpose: Which marketplaces and plugins this machine has enabled. The kit ships no template for it.
files.edit: Nothing by hand for the kit; use claude plugin commands.
files.keep: The Bearing marketplace entry and enabledPlugins for bearing.
files.note: Managed by Claude Code. Look at yours with: claude plugin list

scopes.title: Every repository
scopes.summary: Committed with the code. new-repo writes them for a new repository; onboard-repo adds them to an existing one without overwriting anything (a conflict lands beside the file as <file>.bearing-new).

files.purpose: The standard every coding agent reads on every turn, kept to about 700 tokens: the ground rules, how work is done here, and the report shape. Each step's detail lives in its skill. Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Copilot read it natively.
files.edit: Only through a change to the kit, so every repository stays on the same standard.
files.keep: All of it. A team may add a "Definition of done additions" section, which definition-of-done reads; make check in the kit holds the file under its size budget.

files.installedBy: new-repo or onboard-repo, which fill the snapshot placeholders (__STACK__ and the rest).
files.purpose: Claude Code specifics for this repository: imports AGENTS.md, then a short snapshot of the project, what the hooks do, and what the agent gets wrong here.
files.edit: The snapshot and the list of things the agent gets wrong in this repository. Keep it under 40 lines: it loads on every turn.

files.installedBy: new-repo or onboard-repo; generated from the guard's verb table.
files.purpose: Least-privilege permissions for everyone working in the repository: read-only tools and make targets allowed, commits and dependency changes ask, publishing, history rewrites, deploys and secrets denied. Also names the Bearing marketplace so a fresh clone offers to install it.
files.edit: Add an allow for a tool the repository genuinely needs.
files.keep: The deny list. A personal need goes in .claude/settings.local.json, which must not loosen it.

files.installedBy: You, when you need it. Git-ignored (the kit's .gitignore lines add it).
files.purpose: Your personal permissions for this one repository.
files.edit: Add allows for tools you use here.
files.keep: Never a deny removed, never a loosening of the committed settings.

files.purpose: Rules for source code, loaded only when a source file is touched (see its paths list).
files.edit: Through a change to the kit.
files.keep: The paths list, which keeps it out of context until it applies.

files.purpose: Rules for migrations, SQL and repositories, loaded when one is touched.
files.edit: Through a change to the kit.

files.purpose: Rules for tests, loaded when a test file is touched.
files.edit: Through a change to the kit.

files.purpose: Security rules. It has no paths list, so it loads in every session.
files.edit: Through a change to the kit.

files.purpose: Health, logging and tracing rules. No paths list, so it loads in every session.
files.edit: Through a change to the kit.

files.purpose: Product analytics rules. No paths list, so it loads in every session.
files.edit: Through a change to the kit.

files.installedBy: new-repo, onboard-repo or git-hooks; make setup points core.hooksPath at .githooks.
files.purpose: Asks a person to type the branch name before any push, refuses a push to the trunk, runs make check. This is what keeps an agent from pushing on every harness.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.purpose: Conventional Commits, the task id, no AI attribution trailer, no em dash.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.purpose: Formats, lints and scans staged files for secrets.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.purpose: Shared functions for the three hooks.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.purpose: Points core.hooksPath at .githooks; make setup runs it.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.installedBy: new-repo or onboard-repo append these lines to the repository's .gitignore.
files.purpose: Keeps scratch files, session handoff state and personal Claude settings out of commits.
files.edit: Add the repository's own ignores below them.

files.purpose: Indentation, line endings and final newlines the same in every editor.
files.edit: Rarely; the stack's formatter wins where they differ.

files.purpose: One peer and one lead approve; the standard's own files need the lead.
files.edit: The handles, through company-attribution.
files.keep: The lead rule on the standard's files.

files.purpose: How people work here: the first day, a task from start to finish, branches, reviews, sessions with the agent.
files.edit: Anything specific to the repository.
files.keep: The task flow; it matches AGENTS.md.

files.installedBy: new-repo or onboard-repo; the contact comes from company-attribution.
files.purpose: How to report a vulnerability, the rules every change satisfies, and what happens in an incident.
files.edit: The contact.

files.installedBy: new-repo or onboard-repo when BEARING_GIT_HOST is gitlab or both.
files.purpose: The merge request shape merge-request fills: summary, context, approach, how to test, verification, risk and rollback, checklist.
files.edit: Add a checklist line the repository needs.

files.purpose: The shape of a bug report.
files.edit: Freely.
files.keep: Steps to reproduce and expected against actual.

files.purpose: The shape of a feature request.
files.edit: Freely.

files.installedBy: new-repo or onboard-repo when BEARING_GIT_HOST is github or both.
files.purpose: The pull request shape merge-request fills, the same headings as the GitLab one.
files.edit: Add a checklist line the repository needs.

files.installedBy: new-repo or onboard-repo, with the empty docs/ folders (adr, design, runbooks, postmortems, analytics, security).
files.purpose: What goes in each docs folder and which skill writes it.
files.edit: Add a folder the repository needs.
files.keep: The folder names; skills write to them.

files.purpose: The ADR shape tech-decision and adr fill.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.purpose: The high level design shape high-level-design fills.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.purpose: The low level design shape low-level-design fills.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.purpose: The runbook shape runbook fills, one per alert.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.purpose: The blameless postmortem shape postmortem fills.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.purpose: The VAPT report shape vapt-report fills before a release.
files.edit: Nothing.

files.purpose: The analytics event sheet analytics-events keeps; code emits only what it lists.
